newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran rejects tough EU stance after German verdict.
newsitem.headline: Iran rejects tough EU stance after German verdict.

text.p: Iran on Friday criticised European Union's decision to cut off "critical dialogue" with Tehran after a Berlin court accused it of ordering political killings in Germany.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran, while respecting international laws and regulations in its foreign policy, does not allow the critical dialogue with the EU to be used as a pressure lever against Iran," Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi said, quoted by the official Iranian news agency IRNA.

Europe's swift action against Iran followed the court ruling on Thursday which said Tehran's political leadership had ordered the murder of a Kurdish dissident leader and three aides in a Berlin restaurant in 1992. Iran has denied the charges.

Germany, Iran's largest trading partner and most important Western friend, ordered four Iranian diplomats to leave the country and recalled its ambassador in Tehran. Iran also withdrew its envoy and expelled four German diplomats.
Bonn's move was quickly endorsed by the EU which invited its members to withdraw top diplomats and said it saw no room for the "critical dialogue" it has had with Iran for five years.
"The stance is based on unfounded remarks of the Berlin court judge and pressure exerted by those who are against Iran-EU relations," Mohammadi said.

"(Mohammadi) described as 'unrealistic' and rejected connecting Iran, a country which itself has been a victim of terrorist acts, to acts of terrorism by countries which on occasions have provided safe sanctuary for terrorists," IRNA said.
Iran has repeatedly protested at Western coutries accepting Iranian dissidents which Tehran accuses of "terrorism".

Britain, which has argued for a tough policy towards Iran because of its record on "terrorism", human rights and a death edict against writer Salman Rushdie, said on Friday it would withdraw its charge d'affaires from Tehran shortly.
Sweden and Belgium have said they would also withdraw their ambassadors.
Diplomatic sources in Brussels said other EU members were expected to follow suit on Friday.
